items.title: Section: Subsequently Attained Wisdom — Acceptance and Certainty Across Sixteen Moments of Mind

items.zh: 云何名為現觀邊智諦現觀？謂此現觀後所得智，名現觀邊智。當知此智，第三心無間，從見道起方現在前。緣先世智曾所觀察下上二地及二增上安立諦境。似法、類智，世俗智攝，通世出世，是出世間智後所得。如其次第，於一一諦二種智生，謂忍可欲樂智，及現觀決定智。如是依前現觀起已，於下上諸諦中，二二智生。是名現觀邊智諦現觀。
items.en: What is realisation through subsequently attained wisdom? The wisdom gained after this direct realisation is called subsequently attained wisdom. One should know this wisdom arises immediately after the third mind, once the path of seeing has already occurred. It takes as its object the lower and upper realms' truths as previously contemplated by conventional understanding. Resembling direct and inferential wisdom, it belongs to conventional wisdom, spanning both worldly and supramundane, arising after supramundane wisdom. In sequence, for each truth two kinds of wisdom arise: an accepting, aspirational wisdom, and a decisive, confirming wisdom. Arising thus in both lower and upper realms, paired wisdom arises throughout — this is called realisation through subsequently attained wisdom.

items.title: Section: Why No Purely Worldly Path Can Ever Sever a Latent Seed

items.zh: 此中前智遣假法緣故，是無分別；後智隨逐假法緣故，是有分別。又前智於依止中，能斷見斷煩惱隨眠；後智思惟所緣故，令彼所斷更不復起。又前智能進趣修道中出世斷道，第二智能進趣世出世斷道。無有純世間道能永害隨眠。由世間道是曾習故，相執所引故。如相執所引，如是亦不能泯伏諸相；如不能泯伏諸相，如是亦不能永害麁重。是故彼道無有永害諸隨眠義。
items.en: Direct wisdom, releasing the provisional as its object, is free of discrimination; subsequently attained wisdom, following the provisional as its object, retains discrimination. Direct wisdom severs the latent afflictive seeds within its own basis; subsequently attained wisdom, reflecting on its object, prevents what has been severed from recurring. Direct wisdom advances the supramundane path of severance; the second advances a path spanning both worldly and supramundane. No purely worldly path can ever permanently destroy a latent seed, since the worldly path remains habitually reinforced and drawn along by conceptual grasping — as it is drawn along by such grasping, so it cannot dissolve conceptual marks; as it cannot dissolve conceptual marks, so it cannot permanently destroy underlying heaviness. Therefore that path has no capacity to permanently destroy any latent seed.

items.title: Section: Ultimate Realisation at Last — Exhaustion-Wisdom, No-Further-Arising Wisdom, and the Four Truths Fully Explained

items.zh: 云何名為究竟現觀？謂由永斷修所斷故，所有盡智、無生智生。或一向出世，或通世出世。於現法中，一切煩惱永斷決定故；於當來世，一切依事永滅決定故；名究竟現觀。何等名為出世盡智？謂若智，於盡無分別。何等名為世出世盡智？謂若智，於盡有分別。何等名為出世無生智？謂即此依事滅因義故，於當來世依事不生中所有無分別智。何等名為世出世無生智？謂於當來世依事不生中所有有分別智。
items.en: What is ultimate realisation? Through the permanent severing of afflictions destined to be cut by cultivation, exhaustion-wisdom and no-further-arising wisdom arise, each either purely supramundane or spanning both worldly and supramundane. Because within this life every affliction is decisively ended, and because for every future life the substratum of existence is decisively extinguished, this is called ultimate realisation. What is supramundane exhaustion-wisdom? Wisdom free of discrimination regarding exhaustion. What is worldly-supramundane exhaustion-wisdom? Wisdom retaining discrimination regarding exhaustion. What is supramundane no-further-arising wisdom? Wisdom free of discrimination that the substratum of existence, its cause extinguished, will not arise in the future. What is worldly-supramundane no-further-arising wisdom? The same recognition retaining discrimination.

items.title: Section: False Brahmins and Their Flattering Trade — Three Places Claimed as Truth, All Stained by Fault

items.zh: 復次，有種姓婆羅門，建立三處為實為諦。然彼種姓諸婆羅門，於此三處住三過失，污其心故；依第一義，彼皆墮在非梵志數。何等三處？一、為養命，二、為修福，三、安立果。為養命者，謂彼種姓諸婆羅門為活命故，於施主前或呪願、或讚美、或序述。
items.en: Furthermore, there are hereditary brahmins who establish three places as genuinely real and true. Yet these same brahmins remain stained by three faults within these very places; in the ultimate sense, they are all excluded from the ranks of genuine brahmins. What are the three places? Livelihood, cultivating merit, and securing a result. Regarding livelihood: these hereditary brahmins, seeking their own support, employ incantation, flattery, or rhetorical narration before their patrons.

items.zh: 呪願者，謂彼種姓諸婆羅門，希求隨一資生具故，往詣王所、或王大臣、或婆羅門、長者、居士、商主等所，矯設呪願：當願汝等所有怨敵皆悉殄滅、橫遭殃禍、摧屈縛錄。又願汝等所有吉祥常無轉動、不可侵奪。讚美者，為希求故，往到彼所，矯設讚美，言：汝勇健，多諸計策，善害怨敵。又於害怨假興讚述，唱言：汝曹如是如是害除怨敵，甚為希有，如汝等輩，世間難得。又於財位久興盛者，矯施讚述，言：諸世間如汝吉祥成就無動，甚為難有。序述者，謂彼為希求故，往到他所，妄興序述；言汝成就善丈夫相，不久定當一切怨敵皆悉殄滅、橫遭殃禍、摧屈縛錄。又若成就如是相者，定當吉祥，無有退轉。又如汝等諸親友家、若施主家，常無有餘沙門、婆羅門於中受施執為己有，唯我常得恭敬供養、衣服、飲食、諸臥具等。彼由如是方便所獲利養，深生染著、耽嗜、迷悶、堅固、保執而受用之。

items.title: Section: Sacrifice for Merit — And the False Promise That Killing Leads to Heaven

items.zh: 為修福者，謂彼種姓諸婆羅門，宣說殺害無量眾生，興祠祀福。宣說祠祀獲常處果。又興祠祀時，召命無量國王、大臣、長者、居士，為欲攝受上妙眾多資生具故。彼既獲已，執為我所，展轉互起凌蔑之心。當知彼有如是三失。
items.en: Regarding the cultivation of merit: these hereditary brahmins teach that killing countless living beings generates the merit of sacrifice, and that offering such sacrifice secures a permanent, unchanging heavenly result. When staging such sacrifice, they also summon countless kings, ministers, elders, and householders, seeking to accumulate abundant fine offerings; having obtained these, they claim them as their own, and grow mutually arrogant towards one another as a result. One should know they are stained by these three faults.

blocks.text: The path of seeing completes itself, and the treatise explains why no worldly path can cut afflictions at the root. Then it turns to the brahmins' claims to "truth".
For each truth, an accepting wisdom and a decisive wisdom arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: this wisdom has verbal marks; it is conventional wisdom.

The earlier wisdom is non-discriminating; the later follows it and keeps the severed afflictions from arising again. The worldly path "is drawn by grasping at marks, so it cannot dissolve marks". Master Cháng Bǎi: marks cannot remove marks; only leaving marks behind can.
Exhaustion-wisdom and no-further-arising wisdom: in this life every affliction is ended; for the future, every basis of rebirth is ended.
Livelihood, making merit, and securing a result. Master Cháng Bǎi: there are nominal, hereditary, and ultimate brahmins; a renunciant should be a true brahmin in the ultimate sense.

The false brahmins seek livelihood by **incantations** ("may all your enemies be destroyed; may your fortune never waver"), by **flattery** ("how brave you are, so clever at destroying your enemies"), and by **prophecy** ("you have the marks of a great man; your enemies will soon fall"), even claiming that in their patrons' houses no other ascetic should receive gifts. They cling to what they gain this way.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the faults are killing, holding heavenly rebirth to be permanent, and clinging to self and possessions.
"Marks cannot remove marks." This is why concentration alone cannot liberate: only insight that lets go of marks reaches the root.

quiz.q: What two knowledges arise for each truth in subsequent wisdom, and is it worldly or supramundane?
options: accepting wisdom and decisive wisdom; it belongs to conventional wisdom, spanning both, attained after supramundane wisdom
dharma-knowledge and subsequent knowledge; wholly supramundane and non-discriminating, within the three true moments, taking the unestablished truth
exhaustion and no-further-arising wisdom, of the stage beyond learning
wisdom of hearing and of reflection, wholly worldly
quiz.why: The treatise says two kinds of wisdom arise for each truth, an accepting one and a decisive one, and that this wisdom belongs to conventional wisdom, spanning worldly and supramundane. Master Cháng Bǎi: having verbal marks, it is worldly; having no seeds of affliction and not born of verbal proliferation, it is also supramundane.

quiz.q: How do the former and latter wisdoms differ regarding discrimination?
options: the former follows the provisional and discriminates; the latter releases it and does not, being higher than the fundamental
the former releases the provisional as object and is without discrimination; the latter follows it and has discrimination
both are without discrimination
both have discrimination
quiz.why: The treatise says the former wisdom releases the provisional as object and is non-discriminating, and the latter follows it and is discriminating. Master Cháng Bǎi: the latter arises by observing the four truths as established in the teaching, with provisional phenomena as object, and so is discriminating. Note the English "direct wisdom" here means something other than in §59.

quiz.q: What does each wisdom do regarding the severing of affliction?
options: the former keeps the severed from arising; the latter severs latent afflictions, for only discrimination truly severs
neither severs affliction, both merely knowing the truths
both sever afflictions severed by cultivation
the former severs latent afflictions severed by seeing; the latter, reflecting on its object, keeps what was severed from arising
quiz.why: The treatise says the former severs latent afflictions within its basis, and the latter, reflecting on its object, keeps what was severed from arising again. Master Cháng Bǎi: reflecting on the four truths, it keeps afflictions severed by non-discriminating wisdom from reappearing. So the English overview's account of the latter as actively cutting affliction conflicts with this.

quiz.q: Why can no purely worldly path destroy a latent seed?
options: because worldly practice is too brief, and given long enough it too could destroy every latent seed
because the worldly path has no absorption
because latent seeds are real and cannot be severed
it is previously practised and drawn by grasping at marks, so it cannot dissolve marks, and hence cannot destroy the heaviness
quiz.why: The treatise reasons that the worldly path is previously practised and drawn by grasping at marks; so it cannot dissolve marks and cannot destroy the heaviness. Master Cháng Bǎi: marks cannot remove marks; only leaving marks removes them; however high the absorption, verbal marks remain in it, and so the seeds of affliction are not severed.

quiz.q: What is ultimate realisation, and why is it so called?
options: entering seeing, the two knowledges arise; afflictions remain now and end only in the next life, whence the name
the joy of first attaining absorption
settled faith after hearing the teaching
severing what cultivation severs, exhaustion and no-further-arising wisdom arise; afflictions now and the future basis are decisively ended
quiz.why: The treatise says that through severing what cultivation severs, exhaustion-wisdom and no-further-arising wisdom arise; within this life every affliction is decisively ended, and for the future every basis is decisively ended. Master Cháng Bǎi: the cause of the suffering result being severed, no ripened body will appear, and no-further-arising wisdom is accomplished.

quiz.q: The English has "the basis for rebirth" for 依事. According to the lecture, what is 依事?
options: it is seeds of affliction, and "basis for rebirth" is exact, 依事 being the cause of birth, unrelated to results
it is a monastic's teacher of dependence
it is the ripened results in the three realms and five destinies themselves; "basis for rebirth" tilts towards a cause of rebirth
it is another name for the store-consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in future lives every 依事, the results in the three realms and five destinies, is ended forever, and one is decisively not reborn. So 依事 is the body and life depending on causes. The treatise goes on to speak of the cause of the 依事 being ended, which shows that 依事 is the result. "Basis for rebirth" reads it as a cause.

quiz.q: Which three areas do hereditary brahmins establish as true?
options: non-harming, impermanence, and selflessness, fundamental doctrines agreed by all brahmins and identical with the Dharma
giving, discipline, and heaven
livelihood, cultivating merit, and securing a result
the Vedas, sacrifice, and austerity
quiz.why: The treatise names livelihood, cultivating merit, and securing a result. Master Cháng Bǎi: before patrons they recite incantations and make wishes, praise, or narrate in order to obtain support; and he distinguishes nominal brahmins, hereditary brahmins, and brahmins in the ultimate sense. Non-harming and the rest are the true three places.

quiz.q: What are the three faults in cultivating merit?
options: faults of speech, arrogance, and conviction, peculiar to cultivating merit, the other two areas lacking them
too little giving, loose discipline, and shallow absorption
killing; falsely holding heaven permanent; and claiming as mine, growing arrogant towards one another
unfilial conduct, irreverence towards teachers, and lack of faith
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is the fault of killing, the second falsely holding heavenly rebirth to be a permanent result, the third the fault of clinging to self and what is mine; and comparing the offerings received they come to bully and despise one another. These three are distinct from the three faults of speech, arrogance, and conviction, though the English calls both "three faults."

quiz.q: The English has "genuine renunciants" for 梵志 and 婆羅門 in the ultimate sense. What is the problem?
options: no problem: 梵志 are monastics, all brahmins being renunciants, so the English is exact, unrelated to caste
it should be "kings," brahmins being rulers
it should be "merchants," brahmins being traders
婆羅門 and 梵志 are also "brahmin" in the same passage; "renunciant" loses the pointed sense of a true brahmin in the ultimate sense
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: there are nominal, hereditary, and ultimate brahmins; a renunciant should have these three truths of a brahmin in order to be a true one. The force of the passage is that a true brahmin is defined by truth and not birth. Using "renunciant" for the ultimate term, while keeping "brahmin" for the hereditary one, removes the word-play the treatise relies on.
